newsitem.title: UK: Caffeine can help fight bowel cancer, experts say.
newsitem.headline: Caffeine can help fight bowel cancer, experts say.

text.p: Using chemicals similar to caffeine to improve the effects of radiotherapy could prove a major new weapon in the fight against bowel cancer, British scientists said on Tuesday.

Doctors from Bristol University said experiments showed that if caffeine was added to bowel cancer cells immediately after radiation, the effectiveness of the treatment was boosted by up to 150 percent.
But the amount of caffeine needed to kill off the cells would prove toxic for humans and scientists are therefore looking for other chemicals similar to caffeine which would have the same effect.
Bowel cancer, which kills almost 20,000 people a year in Britain, is particularly dangerous because its cells can usually repair the damage done by both radiotherapy and chemotherapy.
The Bristol team, writing in the journal Clinical Cancer Research, said they had found that adding caffeine immediately after radiotherapy caused many bowel cancern cells to self-destruct.
Professor Gordon McVie, chairman of the Cancer Research Campaign which helped fund the research, said the findings were particularly significant.

"This kind of exciting lab experiment has to be followed up and we will do so provided we get a caffeine look-a-like which doesn't give the toxic effects of drinking half a gallon of coffee," he said.
"If we can get that (look-a-like) molecule without side effects we'll begin clinical trials in 18 months," he told BBC television.
Bowel cancer is the second most prevalent cancer in the Western world after lung cancer and kills about 95,000 people in Europe alone each year.
It is linked with a diet low in fibre and high in animal fat, excess calories and alcohol.
